name: Dietrich Bonhoeffer
title: Dietrich Bonhoeffer: following Christ in the face of Nazism
description: Bonhoeffer, the Confessing Church and his resistance to the Nazi regime: documented facts and the limits of his legacy, according to the USHMM and AP.

sections.heading: When the church was pressured by an ideology
paragraphs: Dietrich Bonhoeffer was a German pastor and theologian. With the rise of Nazism, he opposed the subordination of the church to a racist ideology. He took part in the Confessing Church and trained pastors at the Finkenwalde seminary, which the Gestapo closed in 1937.

The United States Holocaust Memorial Museum points out that the Confessing Church did not maintain a uniform opposition to the persecution of the Jews. It also notes elements of traditional anti-Judaism in a 1933 writing by Bonhoeffer. Keeping this fact allows us to tell the story of his resistance without claiming that all his thinking was free of inherited prejudice.

sections.heading: Resistance, prison and execution
paragraphs: Bonhoeffer worked with resistance networks connected to German military intelligence. He was arrested in 1943 and executed at Flossenbürg on April 9, 1945. The museum documents his contacts, the help connected with getting Jews out of Germany, and the later discovery of his ties to the conspirators.

The Associated Press distinguishes his knowledge and approval of plans to assassinate Hitler from direct participation in the attempt. That precision matters because popular adaptations can turn a pastor connected to the resistance into the perpetrator of an operation he did not personally carry out.

reflection: Acts 5:27–32 places obedience to God above a human ban on the apostles’ witness. The passage allows us to reflect on faithfulness when an authority demands that we deny fundamental convictions. Applying it requires discernment: a historical biography does not, by itself, settle every ethical question about resistance, violence and responsibility.

Bonhoeffer’s story invites us to examine what happens when a church takes on the prejudices and ambitions of its political surroundings. The memory of his courage becomes more honest when it includes limits and silences. A community that wants to serve Christ must listen to the victims and keep its religious claims subject to the test of Scripture.
review_note: No speech or last words are copied. No operational role in an assassination attempt is attributed to him. The anti-Judaism noted by the USHMM is acknowledged.
source_labels: United States Holocaust Memorial Museum, Washington, DC. “Dietrich Bonhoeffer,” Holocaust Encyclopedia.
Associated Press. “Who was Dietrich Bonhoeffer? An AP Explainer about the anti-Nazi pastor” (January 7, 2025).
